title: NY State Assembly · District 76
area: Manhattan's Upper East Side, Yorkville and Roosevelt Island.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent Rebecca Seawright (D/WFP) advanced unopposed; Louis Puliafito (R), who has run against Seawright in multiple prior elections, also advanced unopposed after Mike Zumbluskas withdrew from the Republican primary.

summary.text: Rebecca Seawright is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election in Assembly District 76, covering the Upper East Side, Yorkville and Roosevelt Island. Before her 2014 election she worked as a state director of the National Women's Political Caucus and in government staff roles. She chairs the Assembly Aging Committee, and her official biography highlights work on aging, disability rights, education funding and the state Equal Rights Amendment.

background.text: Wikipedia lists her as born April 24, 1962, in Texas, and as holding a J.D. from the City University of New York; her official biography does not give her birthplace or education.

Before the Assembly, according to Wikipedia, she was New York State Director of the National Women's Political Caucus and a staffer in the New York State Assembly, and worked in Washington, D.C., including for U.S. Sen. Lloyd Bentsen.

Her official biography says she formerly served eight years as Chair of the Board of the Feminist Press at the City University of New York, and that she currently chairs the CUNY Law School Board of Visitors; in 2023 Speaker Carl Heastie appointed her to the CUNY Construction Fund Board of Trustees.

Entered the 2014 race for the open seat of Assemblyman Micah Kellner, defeating Gus Christensen, Ed Hartzog and David Menegon in the Democratic primary and then Republican-line candidate David Garland in the general election; she took office January 1, 2015.

First woman elected to represent the 76th Assembly District, according to her official biography, which says she represents about 140,000 constituents and the largest concentration of older New Yorkers in Manhattan.

Appointed Chair of the Aging Committee by the Speaker in 2025, and sits on the Ways and Means, Codes, Higher Education and Judiciary committees. She previously chaired the People with Disabilities Committee, the Majority Steering Committee and the Task Force on Women's Issues, and served as Secretary of the Majority Conference.
Serves as a Director of the Legislative Women's Caucus and participates in the Bipartisan Pro-Choice, Jewish, Environmental and Gun Reform legislative caucuses.

Was the Assembly lead sponsor of the amendment adding an Equal Rights Amendment to the New York State Constitution, which voters ratified in the 2024 general election; her official biography also lists signed bills on 3-D mammography coverage, the Clean Waterways Fund and tolerance training for those convicted of hate crimes.

priorities.text: Aging and disability rights: chairs the Aging Committee and advocates for direct support professionals, including as lead sponsor of legislation to establish a direct-support wage enhancement.
Education funding: says she has secured more than $1 billion in new state support for public schools in her district.
Housing: describes herself as a leading advocate for affordable housing and landmark housing-reform laws.
Voting access: says she secured additional early-voting and Election Day poll sites for the 2020 general election and the 2021 NYC primary.

positions.summary: Describes herself as a leading advocate for affordable housing and for landmark housing-reform laws that abolished vacancy decontrol and restricted rent hikes.
Her campaign site lists gun legislation she passed, including a law to revoke firearm rights of people convicted of domestic violence, and says she cosponsored a bump-stock ban.
positions.quote: Rebecca passed legislation which has been signed into law to revoke firearm rights of convicted domestic violence offenders.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she cosponsored the state Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, which sets renewable energy goals and greenhouse gas reductions.
positions.quote: Seawright cosponsored the New York State Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, implement the state’s renewable energy goals for 2030, support disadvantaged communities, and invest in green energy projects that pay prevailing wages.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she opposed repeal of New York City’s residential floor-area-ratio cap and supports capping building heights.
positions.quote: Rebecca has strenuously opposed the repeal of New York City’s cap on residential floor-area-ratio (FAR) in the multiple dwelling law which would allow for more out-of-scale buildings.

record.text: Assembly committee assignments for 2025-2026: Chair of the Aging Committee, plus Codes, Higher Education, Judiciary and Ways and Means.
Was the Assembly's lead sponsor of the state Equal Rights Amendment; voters ratified it as a ballot referendum in the 2024 general election.
Sponsors the "Teach LGBT" curriculum bill directing the state Education Department to develop curriculum on the historical treatment and contributions of LGBT people in America.

Says her bills requiring hate-crime offenders to undergo tolerance training as a sentencing condition, reinstating the Clean Waterways Fund, capping annual lender fees, and requiring health insurance to cover 3-D mammography at no cost, have been signed into law.

candidates.name: Louis Puliafito
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after Mike Zumbluskas withdrew.

summary.text: Louis (Lou) Puliafito is the Republican nominee for Assembly District 76 and has run for office several times before, including this seat in 2018 and 2020, state Senate District 28 in 2024 and Manhattan Borough President in 2021. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes a 25-year information technology career at Merrill Lynch and New York Life and 20 years in SEIU 32BJ residential service, including eight as a shop steward. He has not held elected office.

background.text: Born in New York City, according to Ballotpedia; in his 2026 survey response he says he was born and raised in Yorkville, where he also raised his family.
Earned an associate degree from LaGuardia Community College in 1985.

Says he built a 25-year career in information technology for Fortune 100 companies, starting in Merrill Lynch's mailroom and later developing financial applications and managing enterprise-wide systems at New York Life Insurance, and supporting charitable initiatives through the New York Life Foundation.
Spent 20 years in SEIU 32BJ residential building services, including eight years as a shop steward, according to his survey response.
Ballotpedia lists him as producer and host of Decent Life.
Lost to Assemblywoman Rebecca Seawright in the 2018 and 2020 general elections for this seat; in 2020, running on the Republican and Liberal Party lines, he received 42.1% of the vote to her 57.4%.
Lost the 2021 general election for Manhattan Borough President to Mark Levine and the 2024 general election for state Senate District 28 to Liz Krueger.

priorities.text: Open primaries: says allowing independents to vote in party primaries would broaden the electorate and reduce the influence of party extremes.
Restricting minors' social media use and returning public schools to a renewed focus on paper, pencil and cursive writing alongside reading, writing, math, science and civics.
Affordability and economic opportunity, government accountability and fiscal responsibility, and public safety and quality of life.

researchNotes: No independent campaign website was found for Louis Puliafito; his positions and background come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response. He has run unsuccessfully for this and other offices several times previously. His 2026 survey does not address the guide issues; no statements were added from his 2024 survey (the passages found did not squarely address a guide issue). No standalone campaign website was found for Louis Puliafito (Ballotpedia links a Facebook page); his positions and background come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response. Biography details are self-reported in his Ballotpedia survey and no independent news profile was found. Seawright's official biography does not state her education or birthplace; those details come from Wikipedia.
